package audio

// ddsonic base-probe adapter: compiled into the unpatched v0.9.1 base only
// (the active tree has audio_probe_adapter_active.go.txt in its place, with
// the same function). It changes nothing in the base: it reads what the
// probe's logger saw.
//
// Observation and its exact limit. The stock provider keeps its requests
// in a map local to its pump goroutine (audio/provider.go, recvLoop:
// `reqs := map[uint32]keyRequest{}`); no code outside that goroutine, in
// the package or not, can read it without changing the SDK, which the base
// stage must not do. The one external effect of a request being absent from
// that map when an answer arrives is the stock warning "received aes key
// with invalid sequence: %d", logged once per such answer, and only then.
// So this counts an answer that found no live request when, and only when,
// the pump has taken that answer; an answer the pump has not yet taken
// (while it is blocked in a write) is not counted either way.

// bpUnknownAnswers is how many answers the provider took that found no live
// request.
func bpUnknownAnswers(_ *KeyProvider, log *bpLogger) uint64 {
	return log.invalidSeq.Load()
}
